title: About
text:
I am a market research and analytics professional with 4+ years of experience in market analysis, forecasting, competitive intelligence, and consumer insights. I am currently pursuing an M.S. in Applied Business Analytics at Boston University Metropolitan College, where I am expanding my professional research background with modern analytical and data-driven approaches.
My career began in market research, working extensively across the retail sector and analyzing market trends, competitive developments, consumer behavior, and industry dynamics. Today, I am building on that foundation through business intelligence, data visualization, machine learning, natural language processing, and cloud analytics, with a focus on connecting technical capabilities with real business questions.


My interests sit at the intersection of business strategy, market intelligence, and data analytics. I am especially interested in using data to understand:

Market and competitive dynamics
Consumer and customer behavior
Business performance and opportunities
Emerging industry trends
How analytics and AI can support better decision-making

I enjoy projects that begin with an ambiguous business question and require transforming data into a clear, actionable story.



M.S. in Applied Business Analytics
Boston University Metropolitan College
Post Graduate Program in Data Science and Business Analytics
McCombs School of Business, The University of Texas at Austin



My professional experience gave me a foundation in structured research, forecasting, competitive analysis, and communicating insights to business audiences. Graduate study has allowed me to extend that foundation into more technical forms of analysis.
Through coursework and projects, I have worked with Python, R, SQL, Excel, Tableau, Power BI, Plotly, PySpark, machine learning, natural language processing, and cloud technologies. Rather than viewing these simply as tools, I am interested in how they can be applied to make analysis more scalable, insightful, and useful for decision-makers.



I am interested in roles that bring together analytics, business intelligence, market insights, and strategic decision-making. I am particularly drawn to opportunities where I can combine business context with analytical methods to identify meaningful patterns, communicate insights clearly, and support data-informed decisions.



Outside of academics and professional work, I enjoy spending time with family, traveling, exploring new places and cultures, and creative activities.
I am also interested in how AI is changing the way organizations analyze information, generate insights, and make decisions. That curiosity increasingly influences the technologies and analytical approaches I explore.

Fashion & Apparel Job Market Analysis

Exploring analytics opportunities in fashion and apparel
Analyzed a targeted sample of analytics-related job postings from fashion and apparel employers to examine hiring patterns, salary information, geographic concentration, work arrangements, and experience requirements.
Tools: Python · Pandas · Plotly · PySpark · Quarto · GitHub





Top employers in the selected market







Job postings by state




Analysis included:

Employer representation
Salary ranges

Remote and hybrid work arrangements
Experience requirements

The analysis highlighted how opportunities in the selected sample were distributed across employers and locations while also revealing limitations in salary, experience, and work-arrangement reporting. The project demonstrates an end-to-end workflow from data preparation and exploratory analysis to interactive visualization and business interpretation.
View Project Repository →

title: Projects
text:
Corporate 10-K Analysis Using NLP

Comparing Merck and Johnson & Johnson corporate disclosures
Analyzed Merck and Johnson & Johnson 10-K filings from 2020–2024 using multiple natural language processing approaches to compare corporate disclosures, measure document similarity, and evaluate different text representations.
Tools: Python · TF-IDF · Word2Vec · GloVe · FAISS · Machine Learning · RAG
Analysis included:

Text preprocessing and feature engineering
TF-IDF and document similarity
Word2Vec and GloVe embeddings
Machine learning classification
FAISS vector similarity search
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)

The analysis compared traditional and embedding-based representations, with TF-IDF providing the strongest classification performance among the evaluated approaches. The project also extended the analysis through FAISS-based retrieval and RAG to explore grounded information retrieval from financial disclosures.

title: Projects
text:
Customer Segmentation & Business Analysis

Identifying customer value, behavior, and retention opportunities
Analyzed Northwind customer and transaction data to understand purchasing behavior, customer value, and differences across customer segments, with the goal of translating behavioral patterns into actionable business insights.
Tools: Python · Pandas · Customer Segmentation · Statistical Analysis · Data Visualization
Analysis included:

Customer purchasing behavior
Revenue and customer value analysis
Customer segmentation
At-risk customer identification
Relationship between customer metrics
Business recommendations

The analysis identified distinct customer groups and highlighted customers showing potential retention risk. It also examined relationships between customer behavior and business value to support more targeted customer strategies and data-informed decision-making.
